title: Neural Pixelate V3 is now out as a standalone application, it's a free tool for cleaning up AI generated pixel art
author: black-magik-studios
selftext:
https://i.redd.it/l6a2yoerisxh1.png

We're back with the v3 version of our neural pixelate model. In this versions release we wanted to focus on accessibility and quality of life. You can find it here, completely free: [https://blackmagikstudios.itch.io/](https://blackmagikstudios.itch.io/)

We realized that needing people to have Aseprite so they can use our extension was unnecessary. Going forward we will be shipping our models with a standalone application.

https://i.redd.it/nofjtiwvisxh1.png

With this standalone applications anyone on Windows, Linux or Mac can download and run our models. We've configured it so you can do batch processing and added automatic scale prediction where our model will look at your image and predict what is the best pixel art scale to use.

We've optimized our inference so the pixelation process is faster and fixed a memory leak that we found.

That being said, we didn't want to come back with v3 without any notable improvements to the model itself.

Our v3 model is more consistent with preserving colors from the original image, produces less artifacts, and creates cleaner more consistent pixel boundaries.

In terms of our benchmark, which you can find publicly on our github repo, here are the improvements.

|Metric|V2|V3|Improvement|
|:-|:-|:-|:-|
||
|Exact pixel match|56.87%|67.28%|18.3%|
|Mean colour error|3.190|2.735|14.3%|
|95th-percentile colour error|12.028|10.390|13.6%|
|Palette violation rate|34.29%|29.11%|15.1%|
|PSNR|28.76 dB|33.15 dB|15.3%|

https://i.redd.it/dyfy9825jsxh1.png

https://i.redd.it/erasnii6jsxh1.png

https://i.redd.it/bnvsubu7jsxh1.png

You can read more about it in our newest [devlog](https://blackmagikstudios.itch.io/grimoire-neural-pixelate/devlog/1708313/black-magik-pixelate-v3-is-now-a-standalone-application), or download the latest version: [https://blackmagikstudios.itch.io/](https://blackmagikstudios.itch.io/)  
Completely free, no subscriptions or catches and your art never leaves your computer. As always we appreciate your feedback.

comments.author: HugoDzz
comments.body: Where is the repo? Is this even open source? [Pixel Snapper](https://www.spritefusion.com/pixel-snapper) is open source

replies.author: black-magik-studios
replies.body:
Hey, from what we can see you're the dev of pixel snapper. We like your work and we've used it before. We're just throwing our hats into the ring and sharing our own tooling that we've been building which we believe solve challenges that we've had with other tools.  
  
No our solution isn't open source, but it is free and fully local nothing leaves your machine and there's no web usage or hidden catches.  
  
Our approaches are different, yours wins in some places and we believe ours wins in others. Ours is a machine learning approach instead of a rule based approach like pixel snapper uses.  
  
When we've tried using rule based approaches we've found that it struggles with anti-aliased or soft edges often it's forced to pick a color between the 2 options where as our model is better at deciding if a pixel is background or foreground. This can result in some more hallucinations than a rule based approach but it greatly limits halos, background bleed and mixels.  
  
AI doesn't do pixel art well and it seldom tries to generate an image in a single scale, snapping tools assume that the pixel art from the ai output are on a consistent grid which is rarely the case our model is trained with the expectation that the AI pixel art isn't going to fit a grid well.  
  
Snapping tools also don't understand what is supposed to be an outline vs background or colors of an image while ours was trained to.   
  
Your solution is going to be a lot faster, won't need a gpu and is more predictable than ours it has a solid place in this landscape, We believe ours is better suited for more messy AI outputs where rule based approach breaks down and will need a lot more manual post processing.  
  
If you want to know about our benchmark it is over here [https://github.com/BlackMagikStudios/pixelbench-expanded](https://github.com/BlackMagikStudios/pixelbench-expanded). It's a fork of retrodiffusions pixel-bench benchmark he released with his "pixel-art-fixer"
